bug.title: Every record signed in the browser is rejected with 401 record-signature-invalid
bug.symptoms: POST /v1/records (and every route that accepts a signed record: threads, consents, reviews, decisions) returns 401 urn:scholium:problem:record-signature-invalid for any record signed by the web app apps/web/src/features/web-auth/sign-record.ts signs Ed25519 over the binary CID bytes (signer.signWithPasskey(cid.bytes)) while the API (record-core signing.py verify_envelope) verifies the signature over the canonical record bytes (record_bytes) No user can submit a paper, consent, post in a discussion, review or moderate from the web UI
bug.reproduction_steps: Sign in in the browser (virtual passkey), open a listed paper's Discussion tab and click "Sign and submit" on a new post Observe POST /v1/papers/{id}/threads -> 401 record-signature-invalid Equivalently: build an envelope with the web signRecord, POST it to /v1/records, observe 401; sign the same body over record_bytes with record-core and observe 201
bug.expected: A record signed by the web signer verifies in the API and is accepted (201); the web and Python cores sign and verify the same byte string
bug.actual: Web signs over CID bytes; API verifies over record bytes; every web-signed record gets 401

constraints.constraint: Do not change the API's signature verification rule (signature over canonical DAG-CBOR record bytes, as in record-core); fix the web signer
Add a cross-language test: a fixed key and body signed by the TS signer must verify with the shared verify-core vectors that record-core also checks

bug.title: Submit wizard deadlocks at step 4: "Continue to Sign" never enables
bug.symptoms: At step 4 (Checks) the wizard shows "Checks have not run yet. They start when the version is signed." and the Continue to Sign button stays disabled forever checks-step.tsx requires a non-null checks report, fetched from GET /v1/papers/{id}/v/{n}/checks (W/submit/checks.ts), but no such API route is mounted, and the version does not exist until it is signed No paper can be submitted from the web app
bug.reproduction_steps: Sign in as an endorsed tier-2 user, open /submit, upload a PDF, fill Details and Authors Reach step 4 and observe the disabled Continue to Sign button and a 404 for GET /v1/papers/{id}/v/{n}/checks
bug.expected: The author can proceed to sign without a checks report; once the version is signed and scanned, the status tracker polls GET /v1/papers/{id}/v/{n}/checks (mounted by the text-extraction bug in this spec; 404 until available, shown as "checks pending") and shows the advisory report
bug.actual: The wizard waits for a report that can only exist after signing, from a route that does not exist

constraints.constraint: Checks remain advisory (PRD PUB-4/MOD-1): they never block signing
Web-only fix; tolerate 404 from the checks route

bug.title: Social recovery approvals are forgeable: anonymous account takeover
bug.symptoms: Anonymous POST /v1/recovery/requests {"orcid": victim ORCID, "new_key": attacker key} returns 201 Three anonymous POST /v1/recovery/requests/{id}/approvals {"guardian_did": guardian DID, "signature": "not-a-signature"} each return 200 and the request enters the 72 h contest window The guardian DID is read from the request body (requests_router.py _extract_guardian_and_signature) and the signature is stored but never verified (approvals.py approve_recovery_request) PUT /v1/me/guardians changes the guardian set with only an access token: no signed record, no delay, no notification to the account owner
bug.reproduction_steps: Create a user with three guardians and an ORCID Without any Authorization header, open a recovery request for that ORCID with a new key, then post three approvals naming the guardians with a junk signature Observe 201, 200, 200, 200 and status "contest"
bug.expected: An approval is accepted only from the authenticated guardian (the caller's token DID equals a current guardian of the account) AND carries a valid Ed25519 signature by that guardian's active key over (request_id, account DID, new_key); otherwise 401/403 problem. Changing guardians requires a signed record and notifies the account owner
bug.actual: Anyone can complete the approval quorum for any account

constraints.constraint: Keep the 72 h contest window and quorum rules unchanged
Regression tests must cover: missing auth, guardian_did spoofed in body, bad signature, signature over a different new_key, duplicate approval

bug.title: Any endorsed user can append versions to, withdraw or retract someone else's paper
bug.symptoms: A tier-2 user who is not an author of sch:iyzu-o4ol-wpge posted paper.version n=3 (prev = current head, authors = [attacker]) -> 201, consented -> 201, then a retraction notice -> 201; GET /v1/papers/{id} status became "retracted" handle_paper_version (submissions/versions.py ~638-664) never checks that the signer is an author of the existing paper; notices.py paper_authors counts every author listed on any version, including the attacker's own version
bug.reproduction_steps: As author A publish and list a paper As a different endorsed user B, sign paper.version n=2 with prev = A's head and authors=[B]; POST it; consent; then sign a retraction notice for the paper Observe 201 for each and the paper status "retracted"
bug.expected: A new version of an existing paper is accepted only when its signer is a consented author of the paper's current head version (or a tier-4 moderator acting under policy); notices (withdrawal, retraction, correction, response) are accepted only from consented authors of a listed version or tier-4 moderators; anything else returns 403 problem
bug.actual: The signer's authorship is never checked

constraints.constraint: Legitimate author lists may change between versions (co-authors added in v2); added authors still need their own consent before the version lists

bug.title: Review integrity: review.commit via POST /v1/records bypasses all checks, sealed reports leak before the gate, reviewer token keyed from JWT_SECRET
bug.symptoms: review.commit sent through the generic POST /v1/records is accepted (201, state committed) from a tier-0 caller and from the paper's own author reviews/service.py registers the review record types at min tier 0; the tier-3, COI, uniqueness and escrow checks only run on POST /v1/reviews/commit These commits count toward the 2-commit reveal gate and the paper's computed status Separately, POST /v1/reviews/commit appends the commit to the log before the escrow step, so an empty COMMITTEE_PUBLIC_KEY yields a 500 and an orphan commit
bug.reproduction_steps: As a tier-0 user, sign a review.commit for a listed paper and POST it to /v1/records -> 201 As the paper's author, do the same -> 201
bug.expected: Every review.* record is subject to the same tier, COI, uniqueness and escrow rules whichever route it arrives by (or /v1/records rejects review record types with a problem pointing at the dedicated routes); escrow and validation happen before anything is appended to the log. REV-4: a reveal is rejected (409 problem reveal-gate-closed) until the gate opens (two independent commits for the target version), via /v1/reviews/reveal AND /v1/records, so no report body reaches the public log, GET /v1/records/{cid} or /v1/sync/range before then. Anonymity: the one-review-per-person uniqueness token is an HMAC keyed by the dedicated settings.REVIEW_UNIQUENESS_KEY (added by the production-config bug in this spec), never JWT_SECRET
bug.actual: The generic route accepts review commits with no checks; the dedicated route can leave an orphan commit on escrow failure; early reveals are accepted and public (with one commit, reviewer A's report text is served by GET /v1/records/{cid} and GET /v1/sync/range); reviews/escrow.py keys the uniqueness HMAC from JWT_SECRET so anyone holding it can unmask reviewers by enumerating DIDs

constraints.constraint: Do not weaken log append-only guarantees: refuse early reveals, never redact log entries after the fact

bug.title: Files of a paper still in moderation are downloadable anonymously
bug.symptoms: GET /v1/content/{cid} returns 200 with no auth for the manifest/PDF of a version in state=moderation content/router.py only applies the scan gate (423 while scanning); pre-listing moderation (tech_architect threat 15) is bypassed
bug.reproduction_steps: Submit and consent a version so it sits in the moderation queue Anonymously GET /v1/content/{its pdf or manifest cid} -> 200
bug.expected: Content is served publicly only when at least one referencing version is listed (or the object is part of a public record such as an avatar); otherwise only the version's authors and moderators (tier 4) may fetch it, others get 404
bug.actual: Unlisted content is public

bug.title: GET /v1/profiles/{did} returns the user's private email to anonymous callers
bug.symptoms: Anonymous GET /v1/profiles/{did} includes "email":"mei@example.org" PRD ID-7 and tech_architect section 12 treat email as personal data
bug.reproduction_steps: Create a profile with an email; GET /v1/profiles/{did} with no Authorization header
bug.expected: The email (and any other private field) is returned only when the caller is the profile owner

bug.title: Uploads need no authentication, have no owner check and are never garbage-collected
bug.symptoms: Anonymous POST /v1/uploads then PATCH returns 201/204 and a CID: anyone can write files into CONTENT_DIR PATCH/HEAD never compare the upload's owner (uploads/router.py ~349-405); the client picks the size class, up to 5 GiB Abandoned uploads are never reaped
bug.reproduction_steps: POST /v1/uploads with Upload-Length and no Authorization -> 201; PATCH the bytes -> 204
bug.expected: Creating, resuming, inspecting and completing an upload require an authenticated tier-1+ caller who owns the upload (403/404 otherwise); a per-DID quota on bytes in flight applies; incomplete uploads older than a configurable TTL (default 24 h) are deleted by a periodic job (the web tus client already sends the bearer token)
bug.actual: Uploads are anonymous and unowned

constraints.constraint: Keep the 50 MB PDF / 5 GiB bundle limits and the tus protocol semantics

bug.title: Write throttle blocks normal Phase 1 work: counts refreshes, upload chunks and failures; in-memory only
bug.symptoms: Accounts under 90 days old (every Phase 1 pilot account) get 20 writes/day; token refresh, every 16 MiB tus PATCH chunk and failed (4xx) writes all count PRD journey 2 broke with 429 "New accounts can write 20 times a day" when the author posted v2 POST /v1/auth/challenge and /auth/verify count against the anonymous 100/day per-IP pool, so behind a proxy ~50 sign-ins/day lock the node out Counters live in process memory: reset on restart, not shared across workers
bug.reproduction_steps: As a new tier-2 account: one 3-chunk upload plus five records leaves X-RateLimit-Remaining 12 of 20 Sign in repeatedly from one IP until POST /v1/auth/verify returns 429
bug.expected: The quota counts successfully accepted signed records (2xx on record-creating writes), not auth endpoints, token refresh, or tus PATCH/HEAD chunks; sign-in has its own per-IP limit sized for a shared NAT; failed writes do not consume quota; counters are persisted in the database so they survive restarts and are shared across workers
bug.actual: Normal authoring exhausts the quota in one session

constraints.constraint: Keep the per-tier daily limits and the X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After headers

bug.title: No paper text is ever extracted: reading, annotations, full-text search, similarity and AI evidence are empty
bug.symptoms: GET /v1/papers/{id}/v/{n}/text returns 0 paragraphs for every paper, including demo papers whose PDFs contain text The paper page reading column says "The text of this version is not available to read here" checks.save_version_text and the similarity/reference checks are never called; the moderation queue's similarity and references are always null; AI agents receive no paragraphs

bug.actual: The pipeline exists but nothing triggers it

constraints.constraint: Run through app.jobs (eager in tests, worker in production); idempotent per version
Trigger from inside the checks module (subscribe to the existing submissions/ledger events); do not edit the submissions module

bug.title: Nothing creates the node signing key; seed-demo reports AI pre-reviews it never produced
bug.symptoms: ledger/origin.py documents that the node key file "is never created"; there is no command to create it On a fresh node, renditions, AI review records, ORCID credentials and arXiv imports all fail to sign seed-demo prints "AI pre-review" for each paper even after logging that none could be signed

bug.title: `scholium verify --node` reports NOT VERIFIED for correctly signed papers (READ-2)
bug.symptoms: scholium verify --node http://127.0.0.1:18000 sch:54jv-wgzw-fnap prints "coauthor.consent ...: has no signature" x3 and "Result: NOT VERIFIED (1 check failed)" The browser Proof tab shows "Signed" for the same paper, and verifying the exported CAR succeeds The node-fetch path (packages/cli/src/scholium_cli/verify.py ~233-245) drops record signatures

bug.title: A formal review written in the web app can never be revealed; reply and rating actions are not mounted
bug.symptoms: The web app never calls POST /v1/reviews/reveal (review-form/README.md admits "No reveal flow") Reply and rating actions exist as components but are not shown on the reviews tab
bug.reproduction_steps: Commit a review from /review; after a second commit opens the gate, look for a way to reveal: there is none
bug.expected: After committing, the reviewer's dashboard/review page shows the sealed state and, once the gate opens, a Reveal action that signs and posts the reveal with the locally kept secret; the reviews tab shows reply (author response) and rating actions to eligible users, per design.md

bug.title: Sign-in verifies against the DID's original key, so rotation and recovery have no effect; tokens survive rotation and live in localStorage
bug.symptoms: identity/service.py ~195-197 verifies the challenge signature against the key embedded in the did:key, not the account's active key After key rotation or recovery the old (possibly stolen) key can still sign in, and the new key may be refused Refresh tokens are not revoked on rotation; refresh-token reuse is not treated as theft; logout leaves the access token valid for its 15 min TTL Sign-in nonce is read-then-set (race); /auth/challenge rows are never purged lib/api/tokens.ts stores the long-lived refresh token in localStorage, readable by any injected script
bug.reproduction_steps: Rotate a user's key (or complete a recovery), then sign in with the old key -> succeeds
bug.expected: Sign-in verifies against the active key (resolve_active_key); rotation/recovery revoke all refresh tokens for the DID (identity subscribes to the key-rotation/recovery ledger events; do not edit the recovery module); presenting a revoked refresh token revokes the whole token family; nonces are consumed atomically and expired challenges purged. Token storage: the refresh token is issued by the API as an HttpOnly, Secure (except on http://localhost), SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to the refresh path, and the web client (apps/web/src/lib/api/tokens.ts) keeps the access token in memory only, never localStorage; CORS in main.py allows credentials for the configured WEB_ORIGINS only
bug.actual: Rotation is cosmetic for authentication

bug.title: Production config check misses unsafe settings; empty SMTP_URL logs verification tokens
bug.symptoms: validate_for_environment (settings.py) refuses default JWT secret, mocks and fake AI, but accepts in production: an empty COMMITTEE_PUBLIC_KEY (review commit then fails with 500), an empty SMTP_URL, a missing NODE_KEY_PATH file, missing ORCID client credentials, a hosted AI provider without its key, and WEB_ORIGINS pointing at localhost With SMTP_URL empty, notifications/emailer.py writes every email, including verification tokens, to the logger and an unbounded in-memory list
bug.reproduction_steps: SCHOLIUM_ENV=production with a strong JWT secret and mocks off but COMMITTEE_PUBLIC_KEY="" and SMTP_URL="" -> the app starts
bug.expected: create_app refuses to start in production listing every missing/unsafe setting above, plus: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL left at its localhost default (it builds the links in verification emails and notifications), and a missing/short REVIEW_UNIQUENESS_KEY. Add REVIEW_UNIQUENESS_KEY to settings (dev default derived deterministically, distinct from JWT_SECRET) for the review-integrity bug to use. The dev emailer never logs token-bearing links at INFO and keeps a bounded outbox
bug.actual: Production starts with broken review escrow and leaks tokens to logs

constraints.constraint: SQLite is the Phase 1 database (spec decision); do not refuse it
Dev and test defaults must keep working with no extra env

bug.title: ORCID OAuth state is reusable and not bound to the browser session (login CSRF)
bug.symptoms: orcid/router.py issues a JWT state that can be replayed and is not tied to the initiating session; the callback is unauthenticated An attacker can make a victim's session link the attacker's ORCID
bug.reproduction_steps: Start an ORCID link, capture the state, complete the callback twice -> both accepted
bug.expected: State is single-use (consumed on callback), expires within 10 minutes, and is bound to the DID that started the flow; replayed or foreign state returns a 400 problem

bug.symptoms: The default fake provider returns plain text; every specialist agent fails with AgentOutputError "agent reply contains no JSON object with a 'findings' list" (findings.py) The meta-report fails schema validation ("body.findings[0].confidence ... got string") ai_review/background.py ~337-353 never passes the code bundle, so the reproducibility sandbox never runs (AI-4) Unsigned fallback review ids "ai-review-cid-uuid" are stored and served when signing fails; the rebuttal endpoint authz fails open when the paper cannot be resolved; the trigger is installed both by monkey-patching transition_version and a subscriber, risking duplicate jobs
